explanation:
Approve P3: outage IVR message, chat deflection, delayed payments breaks and overtime for 30 payments agents, 13:00-15:00 (₹9,768). Best available plan, though it falls just short of the 80% target.
The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 ticket INC-20261001-6607) is driving the surge, led by card_declined calls at 2.22x normal. No plan reaches 80% over the 13:00-15:00 window, and P3 comes closest. It predicts 75.5% service level (payments 68.7%, general 87.9%) and 7.4% abandons, against 38.7% and 23.7% if we do nothing. The outage message and chat deflection cut the avoidable calls, and the overtime covers the rest. Rest of day is predicted at 89.9%. There are no policy breaches and no escalation is flagged.
Trade-off: Cost: P3 costs ₹9,768 vs ₹588 for P2 (outage response only). P2 reaches only 51.9% with 13.3% abandons.
Trade-off: R1 (₹11,976) and R2 (₹12,468) use more overtime but cost more and do slightly worse (74.8% and 73.8%), though they give general a bit more headroom (89.8% and 89.6%).
Trade-off: P4 (₹7,020) relies on staffing and callback without the outage message and only reaches 54.9%.
Trade-off: The no-cost plan P1 makes things worse (29.8%), because the callback adds load and general drops to 62.9%.
Trade-off: Risk to the other queue is low: general improves from 69.9% with no action to 87.9% under P3.
Watch: Payments is still below target at 68.7%. Check overtime uptake: the plan depends on 30 agents accepting. Also watch whether card_declined volume falls once the gateway finishes failing over to its backup site. If the outage runs past 15:00, the window will need extending.

Approve R2: overtime on both queues, callbacks, chat deflection and internal moves lift service level to 81.5% for 13:45-17:15 at ₹14,607 extra cost.
The problem is demand, not staffing. The 12:30 credit card limit upgrade SMS (MKT-2026-951) has pushed general queue calls up 72%, and new_offer_enquiry is running at 5.2x normal. Service level has fallen to 0% with 28 abandons. R2 is the only option that follows policy and reaches the 80% target over the disruption window. It predicts 81.5% overall (general 78.6%, payments 84.9%) and cuts the abandon rate to 4.0%, against 11.5% if we do nothing. Overtime on payments, callbacks, delayed breaks and cancelled payments coaching keep payments healthy even after 9 cross-skilled agents move to general from 16:00. Rest-of-day service level is predicted at 85.2%.
Trade-off: Cost: R2 is ₹825 more than R1 (₹13,782). R1 is also compliant but falls just short of target at 79.6%, with general at 77.1%.
Trade-off: Cheaper options don't recover service: no action gives 59.9% (general 47.6%), and P1 (₹750) actually drops to 57.9%.
Trade-off: P2 and P3 use an IVR outage message without a confirmed incident, which breaks policy CX-01. P3 also only reaches 76.6% despite costing ₹10,362.
Trade-off: Risk to payments: R2 pulls the most agents from payments (9 at 16:00-17:00) and cancels payments coaching. It relies on 10 payments agents accepting overtime to keep payments at 84.9%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: general callbacks run until 16:00, so some customers wait for a call back rather than being answered live.
Watch: Watch how many agents take the overtime offer (28 + 8 on general, 10 on payments); a low uptake is the main risk to hitting target. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against the 5.2x trend and check general service level is recovering toward 78.6%. Check payments service level when the 9 agents move across at 16:00. No escalation is needed.

Approve R1: deflection plus overtime on both queues lifts service level to 82% (target 80%) for 08:15-15:30 at ₹16,122.
General has 9 unplanned absences against a usual 2.4. It is down to 51 agents against 57.6 expected, and demand and handle time are on plan. Doing nothing is predicted to give 55.4% over the disruption window (general 45.8%) with 10.8% abandons. R1 is the cheapest policy-compliant plan that reaches the 80% target. It predicts 82.0% overall, with payments at 83.4% and general at 80.2%. Abandons fall to 3.7% and the rest-of-day figure is 87.0%. It uses 20% chat deflection on both queues, cancels all coaching 09:00-12:00, offers overtime to 10 general agents 09:00-15:00 and offers overtime to 6 payments agents 11:00-15:00.
Trade-off: P4 (₹11,802) and P2 (₹12,258) are about ₹4,000 cheaper but fall short at 77.5% and 76.0%. General would stay below target at 77.0% and 74.0%.
Trade-off: R2 reaches 85.0% with general at 82.8% and 2.9% abandons, but costs ₹18,372, about ₹2,250 more than R1.
Trade-off: P1 adds no overtime (₹450) and actually predicts slightly worse than doing nothing, at 54.2%.
Trade-off: General is only just over target at 80.2%, so R1 has little margin if overtime take-up is short.
Watch: Check overtime acceptance on general first. R1 needs all 10 agents in each block to hold general above 80%. Also watch payments absence: it is 6 against a usual 2.6, which could put its cover at risk. Re-check once more intervals of data arrive, because only one interval has been seen so far.

Approve P4 (overtime, chat deflection and callback): the only option predicted to reach the 80% target over 10:15-12:15, at 81.7% for ₹6,321.
Calls on general are running long because of the CRM search slowdown (P2 incident INC-20261021-5862, searches taking 20–40 s). Handle time reached 646 s at 10:00 against about 350–376 s forecast. Volume and staffing are close to plan. Service level fell to 14.7% with 18 abandons in that interval. Doing nothing is predicted to give 58.3% over the window, with general at 33.8%. P4 combines the free levers (delayed breaks, cancelled coaching, 3 agents moved from payments for 10:15-11:00) with overtime for 30 general agents from 10:45-12:00, 20% chat deflection of balance and offer enquiries, and IVR callback until 11:45. It is predicted to lift the window to 81.7% and cut abandons to 4.3%. The rest of the day is expected to finish at 88.5%. No policy rules are broken.
Trade-off: Cost: P4 is the most expensive at ₹6,321. P3 (overtime for 25 agents, ₹4,575) saves ₹1,746 but reaches only 73.3% with 6.4% abandons, so it misses the target.
Trade-off: Cheaper options fall well short. P2 (chat deflection, ₹471) gives 65.4%. P1 (₹75) gives 57.5%, slightly below no action, because general drops to 26.7%.
Trade-off: General is still below target even under P4, at 69.3%. The overall 81.7% depends on payments being strong at 90.6%.
Trade-off: Payments is not put at risk: it stays at 90.6% despite lending 3 agents and delaying its breaks from 11:00-11:45.
Watch: Track handle time and the CRM incident. If search speed recovers, consider stopping overtime early to save cost. If the incident worsens or overtime take-up falls short of 30 agents, general will slip further and the plan should be reviewed.

Approve P3: overtime for 12 general agents (11:30-15:30) plus chat deflection and IVR callback on both queues, predicted 84.1% service level for 11:00-19:45 at ₹6,804.
Calls are running about 25% above forecast on both queues with no identified cause: no incidents, no marketing sends, normal absences, and all call reasons up evenly. Doing nothing leaves the window at 72.1%, with general at 63.8%. P3 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target with no policy violations. It predicts 84.1% overall (payments 87.7%, general 80.6%) and cuts abandons from 5.9% to 3.2%. Overtime runs as two 2-hour blocks of 12 general agents. Chat deflection takes 20% of balance and payment-status enquiries, and callback runs on both queues from 11:00 to 15:00.
Trade-off: P2 (₹1,764) is ₹5,040 cheaper but just misses the target at 79.2%, and general stays at 71.4%.
Trade-off: P1 (₹900) only reaches 73.2%, barely better than no action.
Trade-off: P4 (₹11,700) gives more headroom at 87.1% and 2.7% abandons, but costs ₹4,896 more and needs 20 general plus 5 payments overtime volunteers.
Trade-off: P3 does not pull agents from payments, so the other queue is not put at risk. Payments improves to 87.7%.
Watch: General is predicted at 80.6%, only just above target. If overtime uptake falls short of 12 agents, or volume keeps climbing beyond the current +31-36%, general will drop below 80%. Be ready to step up toward P4. The cause of the surge is unknown, so keep checking for a late incident or marketing explanation.

Approve R2 (split overtime plus wider chat deflection) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best option available but still reaches only 61.6% against the 80% target for 12:45-14:45.
The card authorisation gateway outage (P1 opened 12:37) is driving the problem, not missing staff. Payments calls hit 240 against 108 forecast, card_declined calls are running at 2.48x normal, and service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandoned calls. R2 puts the known-issue IVR message on card_declined and deflects 20% of payment status, balance and refund enquiries to chat. It also offers overtime to 46 payments agents (13:15-14:45) and 5 general agents (13:15-15:00), and delays the 14:15 breaks on both queues by 45 minutes. Over the disruption window it lifts service level from 19.8% to 61.6%: payments 53.0%, general 80.5%. Abandon rate drops from 35.0% to 13.7%. Extra cost is ₹13,890, and rest-of-day service level is 81.4%. Escalation is flagged because even this plan is predicted at 62%, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). No plan reaches target while the outage continues.
Trade-off: Against P3 (₹14,784, 58.1%) and P4 (₹15,414, 51.8%), R2 costs less and performs better.
Trade-off: Against R1 (₹13,344, 57.3%), R2 costs ₹546 more for about 4 points more service level. It is also the only plan that brings general to 80.5%; R1 leaves general at 74.6%.
Trade-off: The no-cost P1 (26.7%) and low-cost P2 (₹924, 28.0%) leave payments below 10% and abandon rates above 20%.
Trade-off: R2 depends on enough agents accepting overtime (46 payments, 5 general) and on customers actually moving to chat. Shortfalls on either will pull results below 61.6%.
Watch: Watch overtime take-up by 13:15 and the card_declined call volume. If the gateway fix is delayed beyond 14:45, or payments service level is not climbing toward 53% by about 13:45, go back to the duty manager on extending overtime or adding further measures. Also confirm general stays near 80% once its breaks are moved.

Approve R1: card-decline outage message, 20% chat deflection, delayed payments breaks and 40 overtime offers. Predicted 83.8% service level for 12:00-14:00 at ₹15,528.
Payments demand has surged because of P1 incident INC-20261009-3059, where the card gateway is declining debit cards. Payments calls reached 212 against 108.7 forecast, and card_declined calls account for most of the excess. With no action, service level for 12:00-14:00 is predicted at 39.4% with 17.4% abandons. R1 meets the 80% target with no policy violations. Payments is predicted at 81.2% and general at 88.5%, abandons fall to 4.8%, and the rest-of-day figure is 89.0%. The outage message covers card declines only, so fraud reports still reach an agent, in line with CX-04.
Trade-off: Cheaper options miss the target. P1 costs ₹0 and actually lowers service level to 34.9%. P2 reaches only 62.4% for ₹1,128.
Trade-off: P3 (76.4%, ₹8,100) and P4 (80.8%, ₹11,928) cost less than R1 but break policy CX-04, because their IVR message deflects fraud reports.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same ₹15,528 but predicts lower service levels: 80.8% overall and 76.6% for payments, which is below target. Its abandon rate is slightly better, at 4.2% against R1's 4.8%.
Trade-off: There is no risk to the general queue. It improves from 65.5% to 88.5%.
Watch: Watch overtime uptake. R1 depends on enough of the 40 payments agents accepting overtime for 12:30-14:30. Also track progress on the incident. If the gateway fix slips past 14:00, the disruption window extends beyond what this plan covers.

Approve R1: maximum compliant overtime plus free levers. It is the best available plan, but it still falls short of the 80% target (73.8% predicted for 12:30–15:30).
Two problems are hitting at once. The FD special-rate email (MKT-2026-556) has pushed general calls 20–45% over forecast, with new_offer_enquiry at 2.74x normal. Payments is about 4 agents short (35 vs 39) because of extra sick calls. If we do nothing, service level for 12:30–15:30 sits at 40.5%, with 15.6% of callers abandoning. R1 offers overtime to 35 general agents (13:00–15:00) and 10 more (15:00–16:00), plus 8 payments agents (13:00–15:00). It also adds 20% chat deflection of new_offer_enquiry, IVR callback on general, 30-minute break delays on both queues, and cancels the 15:30 general coaching. Predicted results are 73.8% overall (general 71.4%, payments 76.3%) and a 5.2% abandon rate. Rest of day recovers to 84.7%. No compliant option reaches 80%, and R1 gets closest.
Trade-off: Cost: ₹12,495, the most expensive option. R2 costs ₹8,940 for 68.4% and P4 costs ₹7,140 for 60.7%. That is about ₹3,555 more than R2 for roughly 5 more points.
Trade-off: Both queues improve under R1, so neither is sacrificed for the other. Payments goes from 55.7% to 76.3% and general from 26.6% to 71.4%.
Trade-off: P2 and P3 use an IVR known-issue message, which breaks policy CX-01 because there is no confirmed outage. P3 would also only reach 68.3%.
Trade-off: No-cost levers alone (P1) barely help: 41.6% for ₹675.
Watch: Overtime uptake is the main risk. The 73.8% assumes 53 agents accept the offers, so confirm acceptances quickly, especially the 35 general agents for 13:00. Track new_offer_enquiry volume against forecast in case the campaign response keeps growing. Also check that the payments sick-call gap doesn't widen.

Approve P1: a no-cost mix of break shifts, a 2-agent cross-skill loan and IVR callback on General, predicted to lift service level to 82.3% (target 80%) for 12:45-14:45.
The problem is unplanned absence, not demand. Accounts & General has 6 absences against a usual 2.4 per day (2 called in sick, 4 sent home unwell). Agents on the phones dropped to 27 against 33 planned at 12:30, and service level fell to 58.2%. Call volume is roughly normal (+4.7% for the day). If we do nothing, the window is predicted at 79.2%, just under target, with General at 71.6%. P1 delays General breaks in 13:45-14:45 by 45 minutes, moves 2 cross-skilled agents from Payments to General (12:45-15:00) and turns on IVR callback for General. That takes the window to 82.3% and abandons from 5.0% to 4.3% at no extra cost. It is the cheapest plan that meets target and follows policy.
Trade-off: Cost vs. margin: P1 is free but clears the target by only 2.3 points, and General stays below target at 78.3%. P4 costs INR 630 for 84.5%, with General at 82.2% and 3.9% abandons.
Trade-off: Customer impact: P2 or P3 (INR 3,150 each) give the strongest result: 86.2% and 87.9% overall, General at 83.6% and 87.9%, abandons down to 2.8% and 3.0%.
Trade-off: Other queue: lending 2 agents does not hurt Payments, which is predicted at 85.4% vs 84.8% with no action.
Trade-off: Execution risk: P1 relies on callback uptake and break delays landing as planned; there is no overtime buffer if another agent goes home.
Watch: Watch General service level and agent headcount through 14:45. If General stays well below 78% or another absence occurs, move to P4 (INR 630) or P2 (INR 3,150) overtime.

Approve R1: heavy payments overtime plus chat deflection on both queues lifts service level to 73.2% for 12:30-14:30, still short of the 80% target, at ₹14,148.
The drop is caused by system slowness, not extra calls. P2 incident INC-20261102-2029 is freezing core banking screens, and payments handle time has risen to 561 s against a forecast of about 295 s. Volume, call mix and absences are all normal. Doing nothing leaves 12:30-14:30 at 32.8% (payments 19.1%), with 20.2% of calls abandoned. No plan reaches 80% in this window, so R1 was chosen as the best available. It predicts 73.2% overall (payments 70.2%, general 77.1%), cuts abandons to 6.8%, and lifts the rest of the day to 89.6%. It offers overtime to 55 payments agents for 13:00-14:00 and 25 for 14:00-15:00. It also deflects 20% of selected enquiry types to chat on both queues, delays payments breaks by 45 min, and offers IVR callbacks on payments.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same (₹14,148) and gives the same 73.2% overall with no break delays. It favours payments (73.7%) but leaves general lower (72.7% vs 77.1%) and abandons slightly higher (7.2% vs 6.8%).
Trade-off: P4 is ₹816 cheaper (₹13,332) but reaches only 66.0% with 8.5% abandons. P3 (₹8,640) reaches 55.1%. The no-cost options P0 and P1 stay around 32%.
Trade-off: R1 depends on about 55 agents accepting overtime in the 13:00 hour. If fewer accept, payments service will fall back towards the P4/P3 levels.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 13:00 and payments handle time against the incident. If INC-20261102-2029 is resolved early, scale back the 14:00-15:00 overtime. If it worsens or overtime uptake is low, expect payments to stay well below 70%.

Approve P3 (overtime-backed recovery): the only option that reaches the 80% target, at an extra cost of ₹5,496
Payments calls have run 21-44% above forecast since 11:00 (824 calls vs 634.5 forecast over the last 8 intervals), and service level fell to 15.4% at 12:45. The rise is spread evenly across all call reasons and has no clear cause, so we should plan for it to continue. P3 offers overtime to 18 payments agents 13:30-15:30 and 5 agents 19:00-20:00. It adds chat deflection, delayed breaks and a move of 4 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 15:00-16:00. For the disruption window (13:00-19:15) it predicts 86.1% service level: payments 83.8% and general 90.5%. Predicted abandons are 3.0% and rest of day is 85.7%. There are no policy violations.
Trade-off: Cost: P3 adds ₹5,496. P2 costs ₹1,266 but reaches only 76.6% (payments 71.2%), missing the 80% target. P1 and no action cost nothing but predict 72.7% and 73.6%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: predicted abandons are 3.0% under P3, against 5.6% (P2), 6.5% (P1) and 7.4% (no action).
Trade-off: General queue: moving 4 agents does not hurt general under P3, which is predicted at 90.5% against 89.5% with no action. P1 and P2 do pull general down slightly, to 87.6% and 86.9%.
Trade-off: Risk: the plan relies on enough agents accepting the overtime offers. If too few accept, results will fall toward P2's level.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 13:30 and payments call volume against forecast each interval. If volume keeps rising past the +44% peak, or acceptance is low, reassess and consider involving the duty manager.

Approve R1 (full UPI outage response with 55 overtime agents) and bring in the duty manager now: it is the best compliant plan but still only reaches 67% against the 80% target.
This is a UPI outage, not a staffing problem. Payments calls hit 201 at 13:30 against a forecast of about 96–99, driven by 'UPI payment failed' calls tied to P1 incident INC-20261027-4076. Service level fell to 2.5%. R1 combines four actions: an IVR outage message for UPI failures, overtime for 55 payments agents from 14:15 to 16:00, 20% chat deflection of payment-status and refund-status calls, and delayed breaks on both queues. It lifts the 13:45–15:45 window from 32.1% (no action) to 67.0%, with payments at 59.0% and general at 84.3%. Abandons drop from 26.0% to 7.5%, and rest of day reaches 83.3%. Extra cost is ₹12,657. Escalation: 67% is below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02), so the duty manager should be involved. Even maximum compliant effort will not hit target while the outage continues.
Trade-off: Cost: R1 costs ₹12,657, about ₹3,000 more than P3 (₹9,675, 53.6%) and P4 (₹10,935, 54.6%), but gains roughly 13 points and cuts abandons to 7.5%.
Trade-off: R2 costs more (₹13,917) and does worse at 63.8%, because it skips the IVR outage message.
Trade-off: The cheap options do not help: P1 (₹225) and P2 (₹0) leave service level around 29–31%, slightly worse than doing nothing.
Trade-off: Risk to the general queue is low. Delaying general breaks still leaves general at 84.3%, up from 69.3% with no action.
Trade-off: Customer impact: some payments callers will hear an outage message or be pushed to chat rather than reaching an agent.
Watch: Track overtime uptake: R1 assumes 55 agents accept from 14:15. Watch payments service level against the 59% prediction and the progress of incident INC-20261027-4076. If the UPI fix lands early, consider releasing overtime. If uptake is short or call volume keeps climbing, the duty manager should consider further steps.

Approve R1: outage message, chat deflection, callback, break delays on both queues and overtime for 55 payments agents. Predicted 83.2% service level for 10:45-12:45 at ₹10,275.
The spike is caused by the UPI switch outage (P1 incident INC-20261006-6998, opened 10:31), not by a staffing problem. Payments calls hit 213 against 111.9 forecast (+90%), and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Service level fell to 4.7%, with 59 calls abandoned, even though staffing is at plan (42 of 43 agents). R1 cuts demand with the outage message, 20% chat deflection of payment_status_enquiry and callback. It adds capacity with overtime for 55 payments agents, delayed breaks on both queues and cancelled payments coaching. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the disruption window: payments 86.6%, general 77.5%, abandon rate 3.7%, rest of day 89.2%. There are no policy violations and no escalation is needed.
Trade-off: P3 (₹7,575) is ₹2,700 cheaper but reaches only 77.5%, just short of target, with 5.2% abandons.
Trade-off: R2 (₹11,355) reaches 88.0% and lifts general to 91.1%, but costs ₹1,080 more than R1 for a result already above target.
Trade-off: Under R1 the general queue sits at 77.5%, below 80%. Its breaks are delayed to protect it, but it is the weaker queue.
Trade-off: Doing nothing (P0) leaves service level at 29.4% with 22.2% abandons. The low-cost plans P1 and P2 only reach 39.5% and 49.8%.
Trade-off: Staffing-only (P4) costs ₹8,265 for just 52.6%. Overtime without the demand-cutting levers is poor value.
Watch: Track the UPI incident status. If it is resolved early, release overtime and turn off the outage message. If it runs past 12:45, re-plan. Check that enough of the 55 payments agents actually accept overtime from 11:15, and watch the general queue's service level, which is forecast below target at 77.5%.

Approve R1: earlier overtime plus wider chat deflection. It gives the best recovery available (75.7% vs 80% target) for ₹9,762, but it still falls short of target.
Payments calls jumped to +52% above forecast after the 10:55 reward-points email, and service level fell to 32%. Doing nothing leaves the 11:45-15:15 window at 40.4% (Payments 29.3%) with 15.7% abandons. No plan reaches 80% over the window. R1 comes closest at 75.7% (Payments 73.3%, General 79.8%) and cuts abandons to 6.2%. It does this by starting overtime at 11:45 (35 agents to 13:45, then 22 to 15:15) and deflecting 20% of refund-status, payment-status and new-offer enquiries to chat. Rest-of-day service level reaches 85.4%.
Trade-off: Cost: ₹9,762, the most expensive option along with R2. That is ₹300 more than P4 (67.4%) and ₹2,400 more than P3 (63.0%), for 8-13 points more service level.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same but does worse (73.0% overall, General 76.2%) because it pulls 5 agents from General at 15:00 rather than 3.
Trade-off: Risk to General: R1 still moves 3 cross-skilled agents to Payments from 15:00 to 16:00, but General is predicted at 79.8%, better than with no action (61.5%).
Trade-off: Customer impact: R1 drops IVR callback and break delays. Chat deflection steers some callers to chat. Payments coaching from 15:30 to 16:00 is cancelled.
Trade-off: The no-cost options (P1 37.4%, P2 42.0%) barely move service level, and P1 is worse than doing nothing.
Watch: R1 depends on enough agents accepting the overtime from 11:45. If take-up is low, service level will stay well below 75.7%. Confirm the reward-email calls really are Payments demand (the diagnosis confidence is medium), and check whether the surge eases after 12:00. Keep an eye on General after 15:00 when the 3 agents move across.

Approve P4 (overtime + delayed breaks + callback + chat deflection): the only option predicted to reach the 80% target, at 81.5% for 13:45-15:45, extra cost INR 3,336.
General is short on agents because of a sick wave. It has 26.1 agents on the phones against 32 planned, and 6 agents went home unwell after lunch. Call volume and handle time are normal, so this is a capacity problem. With no action, service level is predicted at 62.9% for 13:45-15:45, with 9.0% abandons. P4 combines offering overtime to 22 agents (12 General, 10 Payments) for 14:15-15:15, delaying breaks by 45 min, IVR callback, and 20% chat deflection on simple enquiries. It is the only plan predicted to clear 80%: 81.5% overall, abandons down to 3.4%, and rest of day 91.3% versus 83.5% with no action. It breaks no policy and needs no escalation.
Trade-off: Cost: P4 adds INR 3,336. The cheaper options fall short of target: P3 costs INR 816 and reaches 73.5%, P2 costs INR 2,520 and reaches 72.8%.
Trade-off: Customer impact: abandons fall from 9.0% to 3.4%. P3 gets to 5.7%. P1 costs nothing but does slightly worse than no action (60.8%), so it is not worth doing alone.
Trade-off: Other queue: Payments stays the weaker queue under P4 at 78.5%, just under target on its own, while General reaches 85.5%. The 80% target is met on the combined figure only.
Trade-off: Risk: P4 depends on enough agents accepting overtime. If uptake is low, the result will drift toward P3's 73.5%.
Watch: Track overtime acceptance before 14:15 and Payments service level each interval. If uptake is short or Payments stays below about 78%, consider widening chat deflection or the callback window. Also watch for further sick-home logs after 13:42.

Approve R1: overtime on both queues plus chat deflection, no break delays. Predicted 79.1% service level for 11:30-13:30, just short of the 80% target, at ₹16,800.
Payments calls are taking much longer than planned (handle time up to 479 s against a 313 s forecast), most likely because of a slow internal tool. IT has not confirmed this, so please check with them. Call volume and staffing look normal, so the fix is extra capacity and fewer calls. No plan reaches 80% in the disruption window, and R1 comes closest at 79.1%. It offers overtime to 35 payments agents (12:00-14:00) and 10 more (14:00-15:00), plus 5 general agents (12:00-14:00). It also moves 20% of simple enquiries on both queues to chat. Breaks stay as scheduled. Payments is predicted at 70.8% and general at 90.6%, with abandons at 6.4% against 18.0% if we do nothing. Rest of day is predicted at 90.9%.
Trade-off: R1 costs ₹816 more than P4 (₹15,984), which reaches 77.4%. P4 is better for payments (74.0% vs 70.8%) and abandons slightly less (5.9% vs 6.4%), but it delays breaks and general falls to 81.9%.
Trade-off: R2 costs the same ₹16,800 but is worse on every measure: 77.3% overall, payments 69.5%.
Trade-off: P3 saves about ₹3,500 (₹13,320) but only reaches 70.8%, with 8.1% abandons.
Trade-off: The no-cost and low-cost options (P1 and P2, ₹0 to ₹1,224) leave the window at 40-46% with around 15-18% abandons. P1 even pushes payments down to 21.4%.
